BrightCare: Hey team — during our nightly payroll run we started getting a lot of 429s around 02:12 UTC. Headers show Retry-After: 30. We thought burst credits would cover a 3-5 minute spike. Any idea why it stopped so quickly?

Maya S: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste an example response body + headers? Also which model/endpoint and approx tokens per request?

BrightCare: Sample header/body below (sanitized):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 05 Jun 2024 02:12:18 GMT
Retry-After: 30
X-Request-Id: bc-9a3c
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "burst credits exhausted" }
Model: rdx-large-v1, avg tokens/request: ~1200 (prompt+completion), concurrency: ~200 short concurrent requests, many parallel workers.

Raj P: OK this looks like classic token-bucket exhaustion. Quick summary: burst credits let transient spikes above your steady quota; the bucket has a max capacity and a refill rate. If your burst (200 conc) drains the bucket faster than it refills, you'll get 429s even if the spike is short.

Omar (SRE): To add — our smoothing pipeline also tries to protect global tail latency. When a tenant depletes burst credits, we throttle to the configured steady rate to avoid cascading queue buildup. That Retry-After 30 is from our fronting limiter.

BrightCare: Understood. Is there any immediate mitigation so we don't fail the payroll job? We can't linearize the run easily.

Maya S: Short-term options:
- Reduce concurrency quickly (50-60 threads) to let bucket refill.
- Aggregate smaller requests into fewer larger ones (bigger batch size) — fewer tokens consumed in parallel reduces per-token overhead.
- Implement client-side token-bucket + exponential backoff with jitter to smooth bursts.
- We can issue a temporary burst credit bump for 24h if needed (requires support ticket + approval).

BrightCare: Can you share example retry/backoff snippet we can drop into our workers?

Raj P: Sure — minimal JS pseudocode we use in examples:
```js
async function fetchWithRetry(req, maxAttempts=6) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < maxAttempts) {
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if (res.status === 200) return res;
    if (res.status === 429) {
      const ra = parseInt(res.headers.get('Retry-After') || '1', 10);
      const jitter = Math.random() * 0.5 * ra;
      await sleep((ra + jitter) * 1000);
      attempt++;
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error('non-retryable');
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries');
}
```

Maya S: Also add a local concurrency limit (semaphore) so you never exceed X simultaneous open requests. Works well combined with the retry backoff.

BrightCare: Any guidance on what our concurrency target should be? We have ReservedCapacity not enabled.

Raj P: For rdx-large-v1 and ~1200 tokens/request, try starting with concurrency 30-50 and test ramp. The exact number depends on steady quota + bucket size. If you want, we can run a short controlled ramp test with you to calibrate.

BillingBot: FYI — we can provision a short-term burst bump. Need: account ID, expected start/end window, and use-case. Approval from finance may be required for large increases.

BrightCare: We'll want a 6-hour bump tonight 00:00-06:00 UTC. I'll open a ticket now with the details.

Omar (SRE): Long-term options to avoid this recurring:
- Move to Dedicated (reserved) capacity for guaranteed throughput and higher sustained bursts.
- Enable request-level batching on your side or use embedding/aggregate APIs if applicable.
- If you have predictable windows (payroll), schedule smoothing: pre-warm by slowly increasing rate before the run.

BrightCare: Good notes. One question: how quickly do burst credits refill?

Raj P: Refill rate is proportional to your steady quota. For example, if steady rate allows 100k tokens/min, bucket may refill at that rate up to a cap (bucket depth). The cap is intentionally finite to prevent very large one-off deluges. Exact numbers are account-specific; we can provide them in the ticket.

Maya S: Action items:
- BrightCare to open support ticket with account ID + requested bump window (they said they'll do this).
- Raj/Omar to offer a calibrate session (15-30m) to set concurrency targets and run a controlled ramp.
- Support to consider temporary 6-hour burst credit increase once ticket approved.

BrightCare: Ticket opened #SUP-78921 with logs and desired window. Thx. We'll try reducing concurrency now and report back. :pray:

SupportBot: Support ticket #SUP-78921 created and assigned to Maya S.

Maya S: Got it, I've flagged for urgent review. Raj/Omar — can you standby for the calibrate call at 18:00 local?

Omar (SRE): Yep, available. I'll pull current quota/bucket metrics and bring a quick runbook (what to watch in logs).

BrightCare: We're dropping concurrency slowly. After 5 minutes 429s drop from ~30/s to <1/s. Looks much better. We'll still take the bump as insurance.

Maya S: Great — marking this resolved for now. We'll follow up in the ticket with the exact bucket/refill numbers and the after-action notes from the calibration. Let us know if anything spikes again. :white_check_mark:
